name: VidVerge
description: VidVerge brings two focused video workflows together: create polished product videos or enhance footage you already have.

apps.name: Vidverge Agent
apps.description: The primary agent hub for Vidverge — a premium, near-black single screen whose identity is a living light wave. A multi-trail SVG motion wave (pure CSS keyframes, no video or animation library) dips into a smooth V across the full width with a bright particle travelling along the main path, and it reacts to what the agent is doing: calm breathing when idle, a faster brighter particle with shimmering trails while working, a one-shot sweep that illuminates the whole path on completion, and a gentle amber trail when something needs attention. A floating VIDVERGE label over the wave shows the live state (Ready to create / Thinking... / Generating / Editing / Finalizing). Below it sits the frosted pill Create bar: attachment button, a full-width 'What do you want to create?' input, a dropdown that routes the brief to any of the six studios (SceneForge, Faceless Content, Script-to-Video, SaaS Verger, Video Enhancer, Ads Studio) and a golden Create button — submitting opens the selected studio with the brief prefilled. Underneath, a compact Recent Jobs queue shows up to five projects with stage label, thin golden progress bar and a preview tile, beside a small Activity panel with an equaliser heartbeat and the agent's last few actions. The Create bar now uploads any attachment once, hands the brief and durable file URL to the selected studio's create screen, and opens that studio immediately. Recent Jobs polls the studios' persisted WorkspaceDB projects, reflects real in-flight state in the wave and status label, and opens the owning studio project when a row is clicked.

apps.name: Vergeye
apps.description: Vergeye is the competitive positioning studio: a customer enters THEIR OWN website address and comes out with a researched comparison against auto-discovered competitors and a finished positioning video. Four screens, one analysis object that each screen adds a layer to. (1) YOUR BRAND — one URL in a hero input; the vergeye-ops server function fetches the home page and the /pricing page, reads the linked stylesheets for the site's real colour palette, and gpt-5.6-terra extracts product name, tagline, category, audience, pricing, USP, positioning and features into an EDITABLE brand summary card. The extracted brand colour becomes the app's accent and brands the generated video; when a site paints in a colour space the reader cannot resolve, nothing is claimed and a colour picker is offered instead. (2) COMPETITORS — discovery runs by itself: three Google searches ('<name> alternatives 2026', 'best <category> compared', '<name> vs competitors') through /api/search, then the model names 6-8 real competing PRODUCTS with their own official domains, rejecting review sites, listicles, directories, app stores and social profiles. Each competitor's site is then read ONE AT A TIME (sequential on purpose — eight parallel page-plus-model reads is how a run gets itself rate-limited) into the same profile shape. Grid cards carry the site's own favicon or a monogram tile, an Include/Exclude toggle, and a plain statement when a site blocks automated readers, with Retry; competitors can also be added by hand. (3) COMPARE — a seven-row side-by-side table (Pricing, Key features, Target audience, USP, Strengths, Weaknesses, Positioning) with every cell filled by gpt-5.6-sol from the pages already read, the customer's own column highlighted in their accent, and ANY CELL click-to-edit. Export PNG snapshots exactly what is on screen through html2canvas (cells are divs, not inputs, and every colour in the captured subtree is a literal rgba so the capture is not grey). A right sidebar carries four AI-written sections: what competitors do better, your unique advantages, positioning gaps, messaging improvements. (4) VIDEO — a 30-45 second script and its 4-6 scene shot list are written from the advantages and the gaps, every line and every camera prompt editable, with optional character-photo and product-mockup uploads used as the opening frame. Veo films it through /api/veo/generate-long-video (8s per clip, each chained off the previous clip's last frame, auto-stitched; Veo 3.1 Fast or full Veo 3.1), then Remotion post-processes the finished cut at 1920x1080 with brand lower thirds, the three differentiator bands, one stat drawn from the comparison and a closing CTA card — the video model is explicitly told to draw NO text so the graphics stay exact and re-renderable. Download video, and 'Use in Ads Studio' records the hand-off on the saved row and opens Ads Studio with the script already in step 1. PERSISTENCE: every change writes the whole analysis to the vergeye_comparisons table a second later under an auto-generated name ('Pictory vs 6 competitors'), so the Saved Comparisons tab is a real per-visitor history — reopening one restores the edited cells, the insights, the script and any render still in flight, which 'Resume render' then adopts rather than paying for twice. The table is serverHooksOnly and scoped by owner_key; every page read, search, model call and render goes through vergeye-ops, because a competitor's site sends no CORS headers and the published bundle's workspace token is public.

apps.name: Video Enhancer
apps.description: The all-in-one AI video editor. Two tabs: STUDIO (the editor, formerly 'Enhance') and PRODUCT VIDEO (the merged Product Studio suite — Brand Reel, Ad Director, the galleries and the studio-tools drawer). Studio is agentic from the first second: drop footage in and, before the creator touches a control, it transcribes the audio with word-level timing (Deepgram word timestamps, Whisper as the fallback with words aligned to the measured speech envelope), measures every silence and filler word, samples frames to locate the subject and the near-static stretches, and produces a CUT PLAN — reviewable cards, each with a type (trim / remove filler / cut silence / captions / B-roll / effect / text / transition / reframe), an exact timecode, a thumbnail, the reason it helps, a predicted % watch-time retention (the model's read of the content blended with the local signal estimate), and Accept / Reject. Accepting applies the edit to the timeline; Accept all applies them cuts-first so captions never describe footage that is gone. A chat panel takes plain-English requests mid-edit ('make this punchy', 'remove all silences', 'where am I losing viewers?') and answers with more cards and whole-video actions. TRANSCRIPT-FIRST EDITING: every word is time-linked — click to seek, strike a word or a whole sentence and that segment is cut from the video, one tap clears every um / uh / like / you know / basically / actually, and a cut can be restored (the range is spliced back into the neighbouring clip, so splits, reorders and inserted B-roll survive). AUTO-REFRAME to 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 keeps the subject centred using the browser's native FaceDetector where it exists and a skin-tone + edge-energy saliency pass where it does not, with a smoothed keyframe path, a side-by-side original-vs-output proof, a confidence read-out, and manual / centre overrides; several formats export in one run. B-ROLL SLOTS: silences, long pauses and low-motion stretches are flagged on their own green track; each slot can be generated from a prompt written off the surrounding transcript, replaced with the creator's own clip, or filled from the workspace clip library. PROFESSIONAL TIMELINE: colour-coded tracks (grey raw, blue cut, green B-roll, purple overlay + text, yellow captions, orange FX), a retention heat strip over the ruler, trim handles on every edge, split at playhead, drag-to-reorder, Shift-click multi-select for batch edits, zoom, and per-clip crop (aspect lock or freeform, 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 presets), brightness, contrast, saturation, speed 0.25×–4×, reverse and opacity. OVERLAYS: the workspace logo or any image, dragged and resized on the stage, with opacity, rotation, always-on or in/out timing, SVG MASKING (rectangle, ellipse or freehand polygon with feather and invert), BLEND MODES (Normal / Screen / Multiply / Overlay / Soft Light) and AUTO-TRACKING by block matching — an optical-flow approximation that makes the overlay follow a subject and reports a real confidence score. CAPTIONS: eight presets (Minimal, Bold, Gradient, Karaoke, TikTok Pop, Neon Glow, Cinematic, Handwritten) plus font, size, colour, outline, shadow, position and a vertical nudge, burned in or downloaded as SRT. TEXT LAYERS: animated entrances (Typewriter, Fade In, Slide Up/Down/Left/Right, Scale Pop, Glitch) and exits (Fade Out, Slide Out, Scale Down) with full type control. EFFECTS and grades (Lens Flare, Light Leak, Vignette, Bloom, Flash, Film Grain; Cinematic / Warm / Cool / B&W / Vintage) per clip or globally, and TRANSITIONS on any cut point (Crossfade, Whip Pan, Flash Cut, Dip to Black, Glitch Cut, Zoom Punch, Spin) at 0.1–2s, rendered as real overlapping sequences. Keyboard: S split, Space play/pause, Cmd+Z undo, Delete remove selection, arrows nudge. The edit autosaves to ve_studio_projects every 30 seconds with a backing-off retry. EXPORT is MP4 / H.264 / 30fps at 1080p through veh-render, which compiles the same descriptors the preview used, so the render matches the stage: 16:9 lands at a true 1920×1080 and 9:16 at a true 1080×1920 (the 1920×1080 master is cover-cropped up by the platform's portrait re-encode), while 1:1 and 4:5 are delivered centred inside a 1920×1080 file because the render service is pinned to that canvas — which is also why 720p and 4K are shown as unavailable rather than promised. Upload by drag-and-drop or picker up to 500MB. Still the handoff target for SceneForge and the Vidverge Agent: a video sent here loads as the first clip and the whole analysis pass runs on it automatically.

apps.name: Script-to-Video
apps.description: The rebuilt script-to-film pipeline with Claude Opus 5 as the single director brain: paste a script (never rewritten) and Opus breaks it into independent scenes, deciding per scene how it gets made — cinematic live-action shots on Veo (with a hard rule against on-screen text), deterministic motion graphics rendered in the browser with HTML/SVG + GSAP (eleven varied treatments — kinetic type, documentary lower-thirds, flowcharts, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, timelines, comparisons, node maps, quotes, annotated images — each with its own content-matched palette, never a repeated generic card), real product screenshots inside animated phone/laptop/browser mockups (Veo is never asked to recreate a UI), and reused project assets with cinematic motion and exact labels. Continuity is frame-chained: after each Veo scene the last frame is extracted and Opus reads its visual attributes (lighting, character, environment, camera) into the next scene's prompt, so consecutive cinematic shots carry the same person, place and light; independent scenes render in parallel. After every render Opus checks the clip against its script segment and flags mismatches. Every scene is independent — own spec, status, cached clip — so regenerating one scene never touches the rest, and a docked Director bar revises any single scene from a plain-English note. Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser: normalization, audio handling and the final MP4 cut, no server renderer. On the Final screen, an opt-in Finish step can add ElevenLabs narration from the untouched original script, an ElevenLabs music bed automatically ducked beneath narration and native scene sound, and scene-timed burned-in captions built from each stored script segment and measured duration; generated tracks and settings are persisted and reused. Runs persist to the database at every step and resume after reloads. Legacy projects stay watchable in the Library.

apps.name: SceneForge
apps.description: SceneForge has two faces and opens on the fast one. AVATAR STUDIO (default) is a one-screen HeyGen video creator: the live HeyGen avatar library is paged in as a card grid with an Indian avatars tab first (HeyGen tags no ethnicity, so the tab matches each look's own name, language, accent and tags, and a flag button on any card pins it there) and an All tab with search; the live HeyGen voice catalog loads as a searchable dropdown with Indian voices first and an Indian-English voice pre-selected when the account has one (v2/voices supplies the labels, v3/voices supplies the verdict on which voices a v3 render will accept); a 1,500-character script box with a live count and an Improve script button that polishes the copy through the workspace gpt-5.6-terra proxy; and settings for aspect ratio (Portrait 9:16 default, Landscape 16:9), resolution (1080p/720p), background (colour swatch, public image URL, or the avatar's own backdrop) and speaking speed 0.8x-1.5x. Generate resolves the look's engine off supported_api_engines (avatar_iv, then avatar_v, then avatar_iii), submits POST /v3/videos with fit cover, polls every eight seconds behind an eased progress bar, reattaches to an in-flight render after a page reload, and finishes as an inline MP4 player with a Download MP4 button; the last five renders stay in a Recent panel with poster, script and one-tap download, and a missing HeyGen key surfaces as a plain Connect your HeyGen API key in Settings message. Nothing in it is mocked - every avatar, voice and video comes from the account's live HeyGen API through the workspace proxy. FULL PIPELINE, one click away in the header and unchanged: SceneForge v4 is a talking-head + documentary motion-graphics studio: the HeyGen avatar master carries the film (intro, transitions and CTA on camera) while MIDDLE VISUAL SECTIONS cut in over its picture and the presenter's narration keeps playing underneath, documentary style. The single orchestrator LLM writes the script, then produces a full video blueprint: every middle scene gets a customer-switchable type — AI VIDEO (real generated footage on Gemini Omni Flash; an unchanged prompt reuses its clip), MOTION GRAPHIC (the new GSAP + SVG engine: branching diagrams, flowcharts, timelines, comparisons, list reveals, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, node graphs, annotated images and text reveals, all rendered from a structured spec whose every string and number appears EXACTLY as written — important text never goes inside AI video; scenes preview live in the browser and are captured with MediaRecorder into real video clips), IMAGE (one strong Omni Flash still), or TEXT OVERLAY (a deterministic animated headline captured the same way). The blueprint timeline is colour-coded: HeyGen blue, AI video purple, motion graphics green, images orange, text teal. Scenes are independently editable — switching a type or editing a spec regenerates ONLY that scene, every clip is cached, re-assembly never re-renders finished scenes, and the HeyGen master stays locked unless explicitly re-recorded. Final assembly composites the middle clips over the continuous avatar master: 9:16 films run through the platform's server-side FFmpeg overlay compositor (base narration audio kept uninterrupted), 16:9 films use one deterministic compositing render because the platform's FFmpeg compositor is portrait-only today. Steps: topic → deep-research script → live HeyGen v3 avatar render (resumable after reload) → style → the STUDIO WORKBENCH, one screen that replaced the old stack of step boards: a top bar with a live provider selector (each engine marked ready or not set up, with the reason), Generate All and Export; a large centre preview of the finished film or the selected scene; a scrollable bottom timeline of scene cards carrying a real thumbnail, scene number, duration and status icon, with a right-click menu for regenerate / edit script / replace with upload / switch type / skip / delete; and one collapsible right panel holding Script, Character, Style, Music, Scene Context and B-roll. Generation reports real per-scene progress with a time and credit estimate, and any failure names the provider and its status instead of spinning. Gemini Vision reads each generated first frame for scene context, auto lower-third copy, a colour palette and B-roll search terms. B-roll rides as a MUTED corner picture-in-picture between a chosen start and end time, so the original audio is never interrupted. Export renders the whole film in ONE server-side Remotion pass that draws the title card, lower thirds, transitions, B-roll and closing CTA over the clips frame-accurately, with narration, music bed and any uploaded audio intact, then downloads as MP4. Underneath it the same engine runs: parallel middle-visual production with per-scene Retry / switch type / Skip → audio-preserving assembly, six quality checks, inline player, ElevenLabs music bed under a 16:9 master → editor handoff — plus the built-in Asset Studio (Omni Flash stills attached straight onto scenes, always reused, never re-billed) and natural-language script/scene/style/assembly changes via Verger.

apps.name: Ads Studio
apps.description: Agentic short-form ad engine: product URL + avatar + assets in, a finished professional ad out. A linear 8-step workflow (Product → Research → Angles → Script → Scene Plan → Generate → Review → Variations) with Claude Opus 5 as the single creative brain. Research crawls the product site (plus /reviews, /testimonials, /pricing and /about) and extracts a structured direct-response brief — features, pricing, pain points, desires, objections, mechanism, awareness level and real customer language, each marked [VERIFIED] or [INFERRED], never invented — that the user can correct inline. Opus then generates 8–12 genuinely different ad angles (selectable cards with an 'Opus picks best' judge), writes a 4–7 clip script (Hook → Problem → Agitate → Solution → Proof → Benefit → single CTA) under hard per-duration word limits (4s→9, 6s→13, 8s→17, 10s→22 words) with live word-count validation and per-clip duration selectors, and directs a full per-clip scene plan — camera, framing, micro-action, gesture, expression, environment, lighting, ONE locked voice description reused verbatim across all clips, continuity notes, overlay plan and an assembled production Veo prompt (clip 1 must open on a first-second pattern interrupt, never a static talking head). Generation is an agentic loop: each clip renders on the platform video model with the uploaded avatar as the character reference, Opus vision inspects the take against the plan (action, framing, flow, same character, clutter, composition), a rejected take auto-regenerates ONCE with the inspector's adjusted prompt (max 2 attempts), and the final frame of each clip is read by Opus into the next clip's continuity clause. Real screenshots are never recreated by the video model — they composite AFTER generation inside GSAP-animated phone/laptop/browser/tablet/monitor mockups, alongside kinetic text callouts, review cards, animated stat counters, CTA buttons, arrow highlights, a logo watermark and styled burned-in captions of each spoken line (all GSAP + SVG rendered to canvas, no Remotion). Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser — chroma-keyed overlay compositing, normalization, concat, faststart MP4 — with a progress bar, a collapsible FFmpeg debug log and a download button. A Variations step has Opus write alternative hooks, bodies and CTAs (up to 3×2×2 = 12 combinations); building a variation reuses every clip whose line is unchanged and regenerates only the clips whose spoken line differs, then re-assembles, each with its own download. The session persists to localStorage, so a refresh resumes mid-run. A RECIPES section in the left rail (below the eight steps) is the app's fourth top-level surface, with TWO sub-sections on an inner tab strip. SAVED VIDEOS is the workspace clip library read through the vv-workspace-videos server function, filterable by the engine that made it (Runway / Veo / Omni Flash / Assembled / Everything), each card showing a poster frame, the generation date and time, Download and 'Use in Ad' (attaches the clip as product footage on Step 1). RUNWAY RECIPES holds the Runway-powered recipe templates — Product Ads, UGC, Product Swaps, Multi-Shot films, Localized Ads, Campaign Imagery and Stock Images — plus raw text/image-to-video on the Runway Gen 4 models (Gen 4.5 and Gen 4 Turbo); every generation is quoted before anything is charged, and this is still the ONE place Runway recipes live. The Product Ad and UGC recipes now CAST AND POSITION THEMSELVES: upload the product image and write what the product is (name + description), and gpt-5.6-terra automatically writes the UGC presenter (name, appearance, personality) and the ad angle (the pain it speaks to, one spoken hook and a CTA) into an 'Auto-generated' card directly under the product inputs — each half regenerable on its own — and both are folded into the recipe's own creative brief, so the clip is filmed with that presenter and that angle. The former CHARACTER STUDIO and AUTO-WRITE ANGLE sub-tabs were REMOVED in that change: their two jobs now happen by themselves inside the recipe flow, so never point anyone at them. Opening Recipes parks the eight-step workflow exactly where it stands; nothing in the session changes until 'Use in Ad' is pressed on a saved clip. Standalone — shares nothing with Product Video, SceneForge, Video Enhancer or Script-to-Video.

apps.name: SaaS Verger
apps.description: Autonomous SaaS product video maker: paste one SaaS landing-page URL and the app handles the entire production without mid-flow choices. It fetches the live page, uses Claude Sonnet 5 to extract the product name, tagline, real brand colours, 3–5 actual features, CTA, tone and target user, then writes a unique 60–90 second three-act narration grounded in that identity. ElevenLabs generates an Adam voiceover while three pure-coded Remotion UI mockups are assembled in parallel: branded sidebars, navigation, forms, workflow nodes, cards and analytics using the product's real name and feature labels, animated with a spring cursor, click ripples, character-by-character typing and visible empty-to-complete state transitions. A dynamic 1920×1080, 30fps Remotion composition times the three product screens and kinetic phrases to the generated script, layers them over a dark brand-to-purple gradient, adds the voiceover from frame zero, closes on a full-width branded CTA card, and renders server-side to a downloadable MP4. Progress updates through analysis, scripting, voiceover, mockups and rendering; completed projects persist in sv_projects and reopen with an inline video preview and Download MP4 action. An optional NARRATION & VISUAL MATCHING step now sits between the identity review and the render: 'Add narration & visuals' writes the scene script first, then every scene gets an editable narration box with a per-scene AI rewrite and an ElevenLabs voice preview, alongside a Suggested visuals panel that keyword-matches the narration against the customer's own uploads and this workspace's clip library. Attaching a screenshot or clip drops it inside that scene's animated product shell (and behind the closing CTA card), per-scene ElevenLabs narration segments replace the single voice track and set each scene's length, and when voice generation is unavailable the narration is burned in as an on-screen caption instead. Any scene that has narration but no relevant visual shows an inline warning in English and Hinglish, with a '3 scenes missing visuals' style count at the top of the panel so it can be fixed before rendering rather than after. No stock footage, image generation or AI-invented pictures are used — the customer's own screenshots are the only pictures, and scenes without one still render as pure coded UI. Distinct from Product Video: SaaS Verger is the one-URL autonomous route, while Product Video remains the deeper editable multi-workflow studio.

apps.name: Faceless Content
apps.description: Topic in, one finished faceless MP4 out — no templates, everything written and filmed from scratch on every run. The Create tab is a single clean form: a topic (with a 'Suggest a topic' button), a niche pill picker (Explainer / Documentary / Crime), a target length (2 / 5 / 8 minutes, default 5), an orientation toggle (16:9 landscape or 9:16 portrait) and a video-model toggle (Veo 3 or Runway Turbo), under one full-width electric-blue Generate. Pressing Generate replaces the form with a terminal-style progress log whose lines fade in as the pipeline advances, driven by a 2-second poll of the project row so a reload resumes mid-run. The pipeline: Claude Opus 5 acts as the Faceless Script Writer — it verifies its own facts, writes the body first and the three-layer hook afterwards (cold drop, stakes sentence, peak teases), and follows the blueprint for the chosen niche (Crime: Normal Day → Discovery → investigation loops → the Turn at 70% → Resolution → gut-punch closer; Explainer: short hook → 5–12 escalating segments → held-back closer; Documentary: the Surface → descent loops → a named human core → the Why in numbers → a return to the opening image), returning three title options, a thumbnail line, timecoded VO/VISUAL blocks and a fact-check list. A second Opus 5 call turns every VISUAL line into a camera-only shot prompt — physical verbs, FOV in degrees, white balance in Kelvin, a cut every ~2 seconds, positive-only phrasing and a verbatim 'NO MUSIC. SFX ONLY' audio lock. Scenes then render SEQUENTIALLY so each one can seed from the previous scene's last frame (extracted server-side with ffmpeg) for visual continuity, on Veo 3 or, when the founder's RUNWAY_API_KEY is configured, Runway Gen-4 Turbo through the secrets proxy — a missing key falls back to Veo 3 with a toast rather than failing. Finished clips are concatenated server-side into one MP4. The Result screen is a full-width player with Download, the three title options, a collapsed script accordion with timecodes, the fact-check list, and Regenerate / New Video. The History tab is a two-column grid of past videos (thumbnail, topic, niche badge, date, duration, Download). Dark #0A0A0A UI with #1A1A1A cards, electric-blue #3B82F6 accent, Inter for the UI and JetBrains Mono for the terminal and script view. Projects and scenes persist to the fc_projects and fc_scenes tables.

apps.name: Product Launch
apps.description: Vidverge's launch-film app, REBUILT FROM SCRATCH 4 Oct 2026 as ONE four-screen engine. Everything the old app was is GONE: the brief-driven Studio, the URL-only intake, the pl-* server pipeline, the beat map and motion program, the six-act arc, the 30-second formula, the 34 composition primitives, the scene editor, the version sidebar and the edit panel — along with every template, sample script, demo scene and placeholder they carried. The app now ships ZERO content: nothing a viewer sees exists until the creator types it. (1) BRIEF — five fields, all EMPTY on arrival: product name, what it does, optional website, optional audience, and a tone (Cinematic / Energetic / Professional / Minimal, which picks the palette). (2) SCRIPT — when a website is given, ps-brand-scrape reads the live page and photographs it (microlink, apify fallback); then claude-opus-5 with extended thinking writes the WHOLE film as JSON over /proxy/anthropic/v1/messages: title, 5-7 scenes (headline, subtext, wordRevealLines, visualDirection, durationSeconds, transitionType cut|crossfade|whip|flash), cta, brandColor and pacing, with accent words marked in *stars*. The progress rail is real — one row per awaited promise, measured elapsed time, no setTimeout theatre — and the parsed summary (scene count, runtime, every headline) is shown before anything renders. There is NO deterministic fallback script: a model failure stops the run and says so. (3) COMPOSITION — the real @remotion/player Player runs that script at 60fps in an iframe srcDoc (esm.sh remotion 4.0.220 + sucrase), mounted from lib/filmSource.ts, the SINGLE composition source shared by the preview and the MP4: word-by-word kinetic reveals on spring(stiffness 200, damping 20) with a four-subframe motion-blur trail that drops the instant a word settles, a slow camera push per scene, real transition overlap, the creator's own screenshot sliding into a browser frame on any scene whose visual direction names a UI, a CTA pill, and a dark #0a0a0a outro where the product name scales 80->100% over a fading tagline. Audio at volume 0.65 is always wired in. data-ui-id on Navbar, Hero, SceneTitle, WordReveal, FeatureCard, ProductShot, CTAButton and OutroCard. (4) REVIEW — the MP4 plays with an unmute button and a true blob Download MP4; 24 frames are pulled back out of the finished file via /api/video/frames, stitched into ONE contact sheet on a canvas, and read by a single claude-opus-5 VISION call returning { score, issues, suggestions }; a score below 7 offers a regenerate, and Regenerate returns to screen 1 with every field preserved. GEOMETRY FACT: the preview runs at 60fps but /api/render/remotion is pinned to 1920x1080 @ 30fps, so the MP4 exports at 30fps — every animation is written in seconds via useVideoConfig().fps, so the two mounts are temporally identical. Verified by probe renders on 4 Oct 2026. Files: App.tsx, lib/{launchTypes,filmTiming,filmSource,opusClient,playerFrame,renderPipeline}.ts, components/{LaunchUi,IntakeScreen,GenerateScreen,ComposeScreen,ReviewScreen}.tsx. Models: claude-opus-5 for BOTH the script and the vision pass; no other model id appears anywhere in the app. No WorkspaceDB persistence — a run lives in screen state, which is why Regenerate keeps the brief.

apps.name: Short Video Enhancer
apps.description: Turn a vertical clip into a finished short. Upload an MP4, MOV or WEBM and the app transcribes it for word-level caption timing, samples five frames for a Gemini Vision scene read, measures the audio tempo and energy, and checks whether the first three seconds actually move. DYNAMIC CAPTIONS are word-by-word: each word pops from 0.8 to 1.0 over 80ms, the current word carries the highlight colour while words already spoken fade back to 50%, in four styles (Bold Sans, Gradient, Outlined, Boxed), auto-fitted so a line never crosses the safe margins, and holding through detected silences instead of running ahead of the speech. There is no caption plate: the words sit directly on the picture, with an optional small per-word pill. MUSIC is agent-written rather than a preset - the scene read plus the measured tempo and energy become a descriptive ElevenLabs prompt, and the generated bed is mixed UNDER the original audio (original 100%, music 25% by default, each on its own slider) with the prompt left editable for a regenerate. B-ROLL overlays the main clip as a corner picture-in-picture, a 50/50 split or a full-frame opacity blend, from the creator's own upload or Pexels stock, and is always silent so the original audio is never interrupted; clips sit on their own timeline and can be pinned to a caption keyword. GRAPHIC CARDS add a title-card hook, lower thirds and a closing CTA. An OPTIMIZATION CHECKLIST scores the short against short-form best practice (hook, captions, music, CTA, B-roll) and offers a one-click fix for each gap. EXPORT composes everything server-side with Remotion through the sve-render function - base video, captions, B-roll, cards and the music mix in one frame-accurate 1080x1920 H.264 master - then offers a full-quality download plus a smaller share-sized re-encode, both labelled with their real measured file size. Every edit is undo/redo-able (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) and autosaves to svenhancer_projects every 30 seconds, so a reload picks the draft back up.

apps.name: Voice Studio
apps.description: Full-stack AI voice and avatar creation — seven standalone modules behind one dark, violet-accented tab rail (sidebar on desktop, a scrolling strip on mobile). TEXT TO SPEECH: a large script box that handles English, Devanagari Hindi and romanised Hinglish, a searchable voice dropdown where Indian voices are badged 🇮🇳 and sorted first (matched on each voice's own accent and description labels and its name, never guessed from a premade American voice, with a flag button on any row to add or remove the badge by hand) and every voice auditionable from its real ElevenLabs sample before a credit is spent, stability / similarity / style sliders plus a speaker-boost toggle, a model picker (Multilingual v2 default, Turbo v2.5, Flash v2.5) and an output-format picker (MP3 128 default, MP3 192, PCM 44.1kHz and PCM 24kHz, each PCM option wrapped in a WAV header so it plays and downloads) — then an in-browser waveform player with Download. VOICE CLONE: drag in up to five MP3/WAV/M4A/AAC/FLAC/OGG/WEBM samples (10 MB each, 25 MB total), name the voice, and the new voice_id appears with a copy button and in every voice dropdown in the app immediately; existing clones are listed with their description and a delete button. SPEECH TO SPEECH: upload a take, pick a target voice, keep the words, timing and emotion and swap only the timbre, with a remove-background-noise toggle and the same delivery sliders. DUBBING & TRANSLATION: upload a video/audio file (up to 50 MB, stored in workspace storage) or paste a public URL, pick a target language from a two-group list — ElevenLabs' documented 29 Core languages, then an Extended group (Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, Vietnamese, Hebrew, Hungarian, Norwegian) whose availability depends on the plan behind the key — set the source language (auto-detect by default) and speaker count (auto, or 1–5), toggle the free-tier watermark, then watch a four-row progress rail with a real elapsed-time progress bar while the job is polled every 5 seconds, and download the dubbed track when it lands. SOUND EFFECTS: a prompt box with Indian-context examples (busy Mumbai street, monsoon thunder on a tin roof, stadium roar, dhol intro hit), a 0.5–22s duration slider or model-chosen length, and a prompt-influence slider. AI MUSIC: describe a bed (Bollywood fusion, cinematic suspense, lo-fi, reel drop) with a length slider up to 5 minutes, an instrumental-only toggle and an engine toggle between ElevenLabs (exact length) and Google Lyria. AVATAR LIP-SYNC: the full ElevenLabs → HeyGen pipeline — script, voice, then a thumbnail grid of the account's live HeyGen avatars and talking photos with an Indian-only filter and per-card flag button, a 16:9 / 9:16 aspect toggle and a background colour picker; the voice is generated first, the audio is handed to HeyGen as a public URL, the render is polled every 4 seconds behind a four-step progress rail (Generating the voice → Handing the audio to HeyGen → Rendering → Done) and finishes as an inline player with Download MP4. ROUTING, which is the one thing to be precise about: speech, sound effects and dubbing run on the FOUNDER'S OWN ElevenLabs key through the workspace secrets proxy, and the key verdict is probed once and latched, with three distinct messages for 'no key stored', 'the key was rejected' and 'the key is not allow-listed for api.elevenlabs.io'. Voice cloning, the voice changer and music run on the AUDOS-MANAGED ElevenLabs endpoints and are billed to the workspace wallet, because all three need a multipart body carrying real file bytes and the secrets proxy's multipart mode carries text fields only. Text to Speech falls back from the founder's key to the managed endpoint automatically, so it keeps working either way and says which engine produced the audio. No ElevenLabs or HeyGen key ever reaches the browser bundle. Nothing is persisted to WorkspaceDB — generated audio and video live in the open tab, and the Indian-voice/avatar flags and clone descriptions are kept in the visitor's own browser.

apps.name: VFX Drop
apps.description: A freeform add-anything AI VFX compositor for the creator's own footage. Upload an MP4, MOV or WEBM under 30 seconds and 50 MB, then type a short request such as 'add rain', 'add neon glow' or 'put fire in the background'. After a 750ms pause, on blur, or when Expand with AI is pressed, the app calls the authenticated OpenAI text proxy with gpt-4o-mini to turn that phrase into a detailed cinematic compositing instruction; the original request stays editable and the expanded prompt appears in a collapsible read-only preview before generation. There are no presets, style chips, preset grid or engine picker. Generate sends the expanded prompt plus a deterministic identity-preservation clause to Gemini Omni Flash, which edits the real source footage while preserving the person's face, identity, body, pose, timing and movement. The browser reads videoWidth and videoHeight after metadata loads: height greater than width produces 9:16 throughout generation and playback, otherwise 16:9, so portrait clips remain portrait. The layout is upload → description → expanded prompt → Generate → result. The existing upload, segmented render, continuity-frame, stitch, credits, refund and MP4 download pipeline remains intact: up to 8 seconds is one shot; longer clips up to 30 seconds render sequential balanced segments and return as one stitched MP4. Nothing is persisted, so the creator should download the result before closing the tab. Files: apps/VFXDrop/App.tsx, apps/VFXDrop/effects.ts (freeform prompt safety helpers), apps/VFXDrop/vfxClient.ts (upload, submit, poll, orientation, credits and download).

apps.name: Video Provider Lab
apps.description: A developer test panel for the founder: one shared prompt, six native video providers, one card each. Every card runs its own independent submit -> poll -> play cycle, so a slow render or a hard failure on one provider never blocks the other five, and nothing in the app holds an API key, an environment variable or a BYOK secret - every request goes to a same-origin Audos proxy path that adds the provider credential server-side and bills the workspace wallet. Cards: Google Veo 3 Fast and Seedance 2.5 (both POST /api/veo/generate/video, polling GET /api/veo/status/:operationId), Runway Gen-4.5 (POST /api/generate/runway/quote first - free, unauthenticated, spends nothing - then POST /api/generate/runway/video with an Idempotency-Key, polling GET /api/generate/runway/status/:taskId), Kling v1.5 std 5s (POST /api/generate/kling/text-to-video, polling GET /api/generate/kling/status/:taskId), Higgsfield on MiniMax Hailuo 02 (POST /api/generate/higgsfield/video, polling GET /api/generate/higgsfield/status/:requestId) and a text-only HeyGen avatar (v3 avatar looks -> POST .../heygen/proxy/v3/videos -> poll .../v3/videos/:videoId, with the engine resolved from the look's own supported_api_engines). Two model ids are walked as a ladder because they are not in the proxy's documented enum: the Veo card tries veo-3.0-fast-generate-preview then veo-3.0-fast-generate-001 then veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, and the Seedance card tries openrouter/bytedance/seedance-2.5 then openrouter/bytedance/seedance-2.0-fast - whichever id the proxy accepts is printed on the finished card. Each card shows a status badge (idle / generating / done / error), a live elapsed timer, the endpoint it calls, an expandable list of the exact request paths it made, an inline video player with an MP4 link on success, and on failure the real error text - 402 reads as insufficient wallet balance and 404 prints every path tried so the endpoint that needs discovery is obvious. Polling is a 5s setInterval cleared on completion, on Stop polling and on unmount; caps are 2:00 for Veo, Seedance, Runway and Kling, 5:00 for Higgsfield (its docs quote 1-5 minutes) and 4:00 for HeyGen. Dark panel scoped to this file only (#0a0a0a background, #111 cards, #6c63ff accent) so the VidVerge shell theme is untouched. Nothing is persisted - a session lives in the open tab. Files: apps/VideoProviderLab/App.tsx.

branding.tagline: Turn any idea into a publish-ready video — brief to video in one shot

agent.welcomeMessage: Welcome to VidVerge. Bring me a product URL, a script, rough footage, or just a topic for a faceless video — I’ll help turn the brief into a polished, publish-ready video. Just need the voice? Voice Studio clones a voice, reads your Hinglish script, dubs a finished cut into another language and lip-syncs an avatar presenter. Want to add something to footage you already shot? VFX Drop takes a short description like ‘add rain’ or ‘put fire in the background’, expands it into a cinematic VFX prompt, and composites it into your clip while keeping its original orientation and your movement intact.
